response.markdown_report:
**Choose a contract-validation audit before further temporal experiments.** At 10% progress, execution failure and absent simulated-user observations justify checking diagnostic and deployment correctness first. Record the actual exception; an audit alone cannot establish its cause.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** First, sampled training errors differ: Electronics reaches 10.38%, versus 0.14% for Movies; this motivates investigation without establishing validation quality. Second, final-item deletion reduces training-prefix hit10 by 0.375 in Movies and CDs, but changes readout content and therefore supports sensitivity rather than a causal explanation. Third, matched replacement retained only 5/1/2/5 users, limiting scope and stability.

**Insights from related work.** First, metamorphic testing checks execution relationships without labels [1,2], but consistency can survive a systematically incorrect item lookup. Second, mutation testing measures detection of exercised defects; surviving faults and genuinely equivalent mutations require separate reporting [3]. Third, sampled metrics can disagree with catalog rankings [4], so implementation correctness and benchmark relevance require separate evidence.

These insights suggest three directions: validate execution contracts, quantify candidate-sampling sensitivity, and investigate internal HSTU mechanisms after basic checks pass.

| Direction | Intervention | Evidence produced | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contract validity | Independent fixtures, equivalent executions, isolated defects | Exercised implementation properties | Recommendation quality |
| Sampling sensitivity | Repeated negative draws | Conditional ranking variability | Catalog fidelity |
| Mechanism tracing | Reversible activation patches | Checkpoint-specific computational effects | Natural causal mechanism |

Scores below are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Proposal | Scores | Originality: positive / negative | Potential: positive / negative | Difficulty: positive / negative |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Contract audit [1–3,6–8] | 4/8/5 | HSTU-specific integration / established methods | Blocks invalid conclusions / exercised scope only | Existing hooks help / independent fixtures and deployed parity add work |
| Repeated-candidate audit [4] | 3/6/3 | Paired category analysis / standard resampling | Reveals instability / cannot remove sampling bias | Cached scores help / eligibility needs care |
| Activation recovery [5] | 6/7/7 | HSTU gate application / established patching | Locates hypotheses / corruption dependence | Frozen weights suffice / fragile internal hooks |

**Selected algorithm.** Freeze each category’s single HSTU checkpoint. Retain identity, candidate permutation/inverse permutation, causal-prefix and independently indexed final-nonpadding checks. Add a hand-computed scoring fixture with distinct embedding rows and an external-ID table independent of production helpers. Test complete logits, including learned residuals; compare singleton, batch and chunk paths, and fresh-process generated-predictor reloads [6–8]. Preserve absolute positions in prefix comparisons; never assume padding-shift equivalence.

Use predeclared float32 tolerances, report maximum errors and top-10 differences, and distinguish score from ranking equivalence. Inject isolated mapping, routing, readout and execution-path defects; mutate causal masking only through supported hooks. Report the detection matrix, false alarms, applicability, coverage and runtime.

Retain the diagnostic API and fixed four-category benchmark. Use isolated diagnostic data rather than consuming the training loader; restore modes, RNG and hooks. Passing establishes exercised contracts, not preferences, absence of shortcuts, or validation improvement. Host macro validation HR@10 remains the selection criterion.

References: [1] doi:10.1016/j.infsof.2024.107410; [2] PMCID:PMC3082144; [3] doi:10.1016/j.infsof.2025.107807 and arXiv:2103.01341; [4] Krichene–Rendle, *On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation*; [5] ICLR 2024 activation-patching best practices; [6] PyTorch numerical accuracy; [7] serialization; [8] SDPA documentation.

idea.description: Strengthen the existing HSTU metamorphic and mutation-testing audit with independent scoring fixtures, complete-logit causality checks, isolated diagnostic data, and parity through the actual generated predictor. Preserve one independently trained checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: Execution failure remains unresolved and no simulated-user observations are available. Earlier sensitivity measurements have limited matched support. Metamorphic consistency alone can miss shared semantic errors, such as consistently scoring the wrong embedding row; independent expected values and deployed-predictor parity provide complementary evidence before further behavioral interpretation.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), all ModelView interfaces, and existing measured probes. Record the execution exception, traceback and failing stage when available; do not infer the failure cause from prior metrics. No empirical pass rate or validation improvement is claimed.

Use the actual trained HSTU model, ordinary-item training positions, and complete scoring path, including the jointly trained lexical residual. Do not assume that predict_score accepts identical shapes for pairwise and candidate-matrix scoring. Document its actual contract and explicitly adapt shapes. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items). Check final readout against features gathered at the greatest occupied absolute index. Require access to the production readout callable; otherwise return null with a reason. Never compare a helper with itself or use count-1 for left-padded histories. Include short and heavily padded histories; separately document the baseline's empty-history policy.

Construct an independent scoring oracle using a tiny, isolated, unfitted scoring fixture with distinct hand-assigned item rows, known features and an explicit external-ID-to-row table. Calculate expected scores directly from the documented scoring equation without production mapping or scoring helpers. Exercise both backbone and residual contributions, including a nonzero residual case when supported. If the complete scoring equation or residual interface is unavailable, report partial oracle coverage and its exact limitation. The fixture is a unit-test object, never a fitted predictor, checkpoint, recommendation source or score-fusion component. A synthetic fixture cannot by itself establish that real dataset mappings are correct: also check category routing, mapping round trips, row bounds, padding/reserved-token exclusions and checkpoint/category metadata using the current trial's public mappings.

For candidate permutation checks, invert the permutation on the candidate axis before comparison. For candidate-independent scoring, compare singleton, batched and chunked execution with the same histories and ordered candidates. Use batch sizes 1 and 3 and chunk sizes 1, 7 and the full candidate count, including a nondivisible final chunk. Use deliberately different histories across batch rows to expose broadcasting defects. If candidate or batch dependence is intentional, report that contract and mark incompatible equivalence checks inapplicable rather than declaring a defect automatically.

For causality, select valid next-item position t and hold sequence[:t+1] and candidate IDs fixed. Change only occupied item positions strictly after t, leaving padding and positions unchanged. Compare features through t and complete logits at t; later branches, pooling and residuals must not leak future tokens. Compare against a prefix-only execution only when the original effective absolute position IDs, masks and normalization semantics can be preserved. A compacted prefix with shifted learned absolute positions is not an equivalent control. Inspect attention-mask conventions in the actual HSTU implementation. Where functional SDPA is used, boolean True means allowed attention and evaluation must explicitly supply dropout_p=0.0. Do not assume SDPA exists merely from the model family.

Before saving, capture deterministic float32 reference logits in evaluation mode for a fixed training-only fixture suite. After the normal checkpoint and predictor writer run, reconstruct the single category model in a fresh process through the actual generated working/predict.py path, with identical inputs and ordered candidates. Compare complete logits, mappings, category routing, top-10 membership and rankings; backbone-feature or rank parity alone is insufficient. Invoke an existing raw-score entry point or share the exact production scoring callable with a diagnostic entry point; do not create a parallel scorer that could conceal deployment drift. If only ranked output is exposed, report logit parity unavailable until that entry point is provided. Ensure residual parameters and inference-dependent tensors are registered in state_dict or explicitly reconstructed from trial-local artifacts. Strictly load the expected state and report missing or unexpected keys. Fresh-process reload uses the same checkpoint and is not another fitted model.

Predeclare primary parity checks in float32 on the same device, software stack and backend, with autocast disabled, atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4. These are proposed protocol tolerances, not universal guarantees. Record maximum absolute and relative deviations and repeated-execution variability. Report raw-score tolerance failures separately from ranking and top-10 differences. Apply the host's documented tie rule where available; otherwise compare tie groups, disclose the diagnostic tie convention, and avoid claiming exact host-ranking parity. Near ties may change top-10 membership even when logits are numerically close. Do not loosen tolerances after observing failures without recording a protocol revision. Other dtypes require separately predeclared tolerances.

Predeclare isolated defects: off-by-one IDs, swapped embedding rows, padding-ID aliasing, wrong category routing, candidate sorting without inverse restoration, batch-row broadcasting, final-chunk omission, count-minus-one readout and, only when safely supported, disabled causal masking. Mutate temporary diagnostic callables or reversible hooks, never saved checkpoints or actual recommendations. Readout mutation is exercised only when padding makes the selected index differ and the selected representations differ measurably. Mapping mutations require affected IDs in the fixtures. Causal mutations require occupied future positions and measurable exposure through the supported hook. Use independently correct fixture expectations to detect consistent lookup defects that permutation tests miss. Record probe-by-mutant kills, survivors, unsupported cases, unexercised cases and equivalent changes separately. Detection means violation of a predeclared relation or expected value. Positive score scaling is ranking-equivalent but not raw-score-equivalent; equivalence always refers to a named observable contract. A surviving exercised mutant is not automatically equivalent. Report per-defect results and any aggregate denominator explicitly; mutation scores measure this chosen suite's fault sensitivity, not general correctness.

Bound the primary suite to eight deterministic training histories per category, selected from sorted eligible user IDs using a local seed-42 generator, stratified descriptively by occupied length where possible. Use up to 100 unique ordinary candidate IDs per history, deterministically selected from current category mappings and including its next training target when available; no held-out labels are needed. Use all eligible histories when fewer than eight exist and report coverage. These fixtures support correctness checks, not ranking-quality estimates. Persist selected IDs, sequences, positions, candidate order, tolerances and protocol version beneath the current trial directory. Log actual executions, candidate scores, wall time, GPU interval and memory. Expand the bounded suite only for an explicitly recorded failure investigation.

Do not iterate an active training loader for the audit and assume RNG restoration rewinds it. Prefer copied, immutable batches previously captured during ordinary training, or an isolated diagnostic dataset and loader with num_workers=0, shuffle=False and its own generator. Record the source; if neither is available, return null rather than silently consuming the supplied loader. Worker processes, prefetch queues, sampler iterators and mutable datasets are not restored by resetting main-process RNG. A future multiworker diagnostic loader must isolate dataset state and seed worker libraries explicitly.

Save and restore every module training flag, Python and NumPy RNG states, Torch CPU and CUDA RNG states, and any explicit generators touched by diagnostics. Use model.eval() and torch.inference_mode(); neither substitutes for the other. Remove temporary hooks in finally, including after failure. Record deterministic-algorithm and cuDNN settings without silently changing the baseline training policy. Strict deterministic execution may be used in an isolated audit process, with unsupported operations reported rather than silently bypassed. Seeds do not guarantee reproducibility across devices or software releases.

Return metrics and metric_definitions with coverage, controls, numerical deviations, mutation applicability, the detection matrix, deployment parity, exclusions and runtime. Missing or unsupported checks remain null with reasons. The interpretation prompt must prioritize failed and unexercised contracts, distinguish measured implementation properties from behavioral hypotheses, and state that correctness checks neither diagnose nor rule out shortcut learning. Training-prefix probes cannot demonstrate generalization; repeated protocol tuning can overfit the audit suite. Fix the suite before inspecting effects and document subsequent revisions. Four-category sensitivity macro summaries still require all four category records; never substitute this audit's pass rate for host validation.

Preserve exactly one independently trained HSTU model/checkpoint per category, all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. No architecture or training change is required. Any later inference change must update the predictor writer and pass parity checks. Do not read other trials, reuse their checkpoints, access hidden tests, fetch weights or use unavailable reviews, ratings, prices, stores, item categories or simulator traits. Diagnostics and debugging consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. The simulator recommendation path must continue serving full-catalog unseen-item recommendations to five real training users per category without changing that cohort. Keep sampled training diagnostics separate from catalog stability and the pinned host validation protocol of 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        saved = save_module_flags_rng_and_touched_generator_states(self.view.model)
        hooks = []
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            fixtures = isolated_training_fixtures_or_captured_immutable_batches(
                active_loader=train_loader, consume_active_loader=False,
                max_histories=8, max_candidates=100, local_seed=42)
            if fixtures is None:
                return defined_null_result('No isolated diagnostic data available')

            with torch.inference_mode(), autocast_disabled():
                results = retain_existing_probes_using_isolated_data(fixtures)
                oracle = build_unfitted_hand_specified_scoring_fixture()
                # Expected values use literal mapping tables and explicit equations.
                expected = independently_calculate_complete_scores(oracle)
                record_oracle_comparison(production_score_path(oracle), expected,
                                         atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4)

                for sequence, targets, candidates in fixtures:
                    features = self.view.log2feats(sequence)
                    positions = arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
                    last = positions.expand_as(sequence).masked_fill(sequence.eq(0), -1).amax(1)
                    valid = last.ge(0)
                    expected_readout = features[valid, last[valid]]
                    compare_production_readout_or_record_unavailable(
                        expected_readout, sequence, valid)

                    original = complete_production_logits(sequence, candidates)
                    record_relation('identity', original,
                                    complete_production_logits(sequence, candidates))
                    permutation = local_permutation(candidate_axis(candidates))
                    permuted = complete_production_logits(sequence, candidates[..., permutation])
                    record_relation('candidate_order', original,
                                    permuted[..., inverse_permutation(permutation)])
                    compare_singleton_batch_and_chunk_paths_if_contract_allows(
                        sequence, candidates, batch_sizes=[1, 3], chunk_sizes=[1, 7, 'all'])

                    for t in deterministic_valid_nonfinal_positions(sequence):
                        changed = replace_only_occupied_future_items(sequence, after=t)
                        record_relation('causal_features', features[:, :t+1],
                                        self.view.log2feats(changed)[:, :t+1])
                        record_relation('causal_complete_logits',
                            complete_logits_at_position(sequence, t, candidates),
                            complete_logits_at_position(changed, t, candidates))
                        compare_prefix_only_if_positions_and_semantics_match(sequence, t, candidates)

                for mutant in preregistered_isolated_mutants():
                    with temporary_mutation_or_record_unsupported(mutant, hooks):
                        record_exercise_evidence_and_independent_oracle_or_relation_failures(mutant)
                results.update(summarize_controls_mutations_coverage_and_cost())
                return {'metrics': results, 'metric_definitions': explicit_definitions()}
        finally:
            remove_all_hooks(hooks)
            restore_module_flags_rng_and_generator_states(saved)

# Host-side integration after the normal save and predictor-writing stage:
# Capture pre-save complete logits for the persisted training-only fixture suite.
# In a fresh process, load the SAME single category checkpoint through working/predict.py.
# Compare mappings, complete logits, ordered candidates, top-10 membership and rankings.
# Record unsupported access, failures, ties, environment, cost and protocol version.


def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return render_measured_metrics_and_definitions(
        raw_diagnosis,
        instructions='Report failed, unsupported and unexercised contracts first. '
                     'Separate independent-oracle evidence, consistency checks and deployment parity. '
                     'Passing covers exercised properties only; it does not establish preferences, '
                     'absence of shortcuts, generalization or validation improvement.')

originality.positive: Connects HSTU readout, complete-logit causality, independent mapping fixtures and generated-predictor parity to explicit defect-detection evidence.
originality.negative: The constituent testing methods are established; the contribution remains a task-specific integration rather than a new recommendation algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Provides a reusable foundation for trustworthy history interventions and future architecture changes while preserving a single fitted predictor per category.
future_potential.negative: Its value depends on actual fault coverage; passing cannot demonstrate improved HR@10 or eliminate untested semantic and behavioral failures.

code_difficulty.positive: Most checks reuse existing feature and scoring hooks without retraining or architecture changes.
code_difficulty.negative: Independent complete-score fixtures, isolated loader state, mutation applicability and fresh-process parity through the generated predictor make difficulty higher than the original rating of three.

related_work.title: 2024 recommender metamorphic-testing study supplied in the search results
contributions: Investigates oracle-free reliability testing across LibRec, PREA and Surprise.
limitations: Does not directly establish HSTU-specific invariants.
Execution consistency does not establish semantic correctness or recommendation quality.

related_work.title: Machine-learning metamorphic testing and mutation analysis study supplied in the search results
contributions: Connects metamorphic relations with mutation analysis for testing machine-learning software.
limitations: Valid relations and mutation coverage must be established for the actual implementation.
Shared semantic errors can survive consistency relations.

related_work.title: 2025 metamorphic-relation selection and mutation-testing study supplied in the search results
contributions: Combines metamorphic-relation selection with mutation testing to evaluate fault detection.
limitations: Adequacy claims depend on applicable, exercised and non-equivalent mutations.

related_work.title: Mutation-testing reflection supplied in the search results
contributions: Discusses how mutant design and interpretation affect mutation-testing conclusions.
limitations: A mutation score does not establish general correctness.
Equivalence must be defined relative to the tested observable contract.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can disagree with full-catalog model comparisons.
limitations: Does not demonstrate a defect or validation improvement in this HSTU checkpoint.
Repeated candidate sampling measures variability without eliminating systematic sampling bias.

related_work.title: Activation-patching best-practices study supplied in the search results
contributions: Examines how corruption and measurement choices affect activation-patching conclusions.
limitations: HSTU application requires implementation-specific hooks and controlled interventions.
Recovery alone does not identify the natural mechanism.

related_work.title: PyTorch numerical accuracy
contributions: Explains why mathematically equivalent batched and individual computations can differ numerically.
limitations: Does not prescribe a universal tolerance or guarantee ranking parity near ties.

related_work.title: PyTorch scaled dot product attention
contributions: Documents boolean-mask semantics and the need to explicitly disable functional attention dropout during evaluation.
limitations: Applies directly only if the supplied implementation uses this function.
A causal attention mask does not establish causality of auxiliary scoring branches.

related_work.title: PyTorch serialization semantics
contributions: Documents state dictionaries, registered parameters and persistent buffers.
limitations: Successful loading does not independently verify mappings, preprocessing or complete deployed logits.

related_work.title: PyTorch saving and loading models
contributions: Describes reconstructing models, loading state dictionaries and using evaluation mode.
limitations: Deployment parity still requires testing the actual generated predictor and its auxiliary artifacts.

related_work.title: PyTorch reproducibility
contributions: Documents RNG seeding, deterministic execution settings and reproducibility limits.
limitations: Seeds alone do not guarantee reproducibility across software releases or devices.
Main-process RNG restoration does not rewind active loader iterators or worker state.

related_work.title: PyTorch inference mode
contributions: Documents inference-mode behavior and reduced autograd overhead.
limitations: Inference mode does not set evaluation mode or independently disable dropout.

related_work.title: PyTorch DataLoader documentation
contributions: Documents loader generators, worker initialization, sampling and multiprocessing behavior.
limitations: Restoring global RNG state cannot generally restore consumed sampler positions, prefetched batches or mutable worker datasets.
